Artificial Intelligence (AI) is redefining #drugdiscovery, #DNASynthesis and #proteinengineering; three disciplines are now converging into a single design-build-test loop. Demis Hassabis's AlphaFold work at DeepMind, was the moment the field saw that biological structure could be predicted computationally rather than solved step by step at the bench, & that moment is what brought AI-first companies and IKP into one room on 28th August.

IKP Knowledge Park hosted Twist Bioscience for a workshop titled "Writing the Future of AI Protein Design" anchored by Dr Ramesh V & Riya Sarkar, Ph.D

IKP's CEO, Satya Prakash Dash opened the session by pointing to IKP's own density of talent: more than 4,000 scientists within the campus, & the startups already building at this intersection.

Four speakers set the pace for the day. Dr. Charlie Lee, (Amazon Web Services (AWS) showed how AI is cutting pre-clinical drug discovery from 4 years to 16-18 months & showed use cases by global pharma MNCs. 
Dr. Aridni Shah (immunitoAI) gave a masterclass of antibody generation with AI-guided design. ImmunitoAI is replacing traditional animal testing with a biology-first, AI-driven platform that transforms input antigens into sequences. 
Dr. Akshay C. (PopVax) mentioned that Popvax is tackling the protein inverse folding challenge by combining generative denoising, direct performance optimization, and rigorous failure-driven learning. 

Bernd Willems, (Twist Bioscience) closed with Twist's own validation of LLM-designed de novo protein binders, characterizing 1,200 binders against 15 targets in three weeks, with above-benchmark hit rates.

A panel discussion, moderated by Dr. Satya, brought the four speakers together with Mark Dupal (Twist Bioscience) that touched upon India's readiness to leverage the AI opportunity. Mark's closing observations stayed with the room: the pace of change he is seeing in Hyderabad & Bengaluru is tremendous, and India is now at an inflection point & has the talent and the funding it needs, provided institutions like IKP keep building the ecosystem around it. Importantly it was a fun day discussing #science & how we will leverage science.

This is the future of #drugdiscovery, & IKP is keen to support the startups building at the intersection of AI and biology. We are glad to be building it with partners like Twist Bioscience.

Can space help unlock treatments for diseases we still struggle to cure on Earth? UK biotech company Mass Balance believes it can. By harnessing the unique conditions of microgravity, the company is uncovering new insights into protein molecules and combining them with AI to advance drug discovery. Its work could help open up new possibilities for treating diseases such as Alzheimer's, Parkinson's and certain cancers.
 
Mass Balance is now bringing its frontier research to India, establishing a presence at C-CAMP in Bengaluru, a leading life sciences innovation hub. The company's expansion highlights the growing opportunities for closer collaboration between the UK's deep-tech sector and India's rapidly expanding biotechnology ecosystem.

Day 3 | Partnerships, Fundraising Readiness & Founder Evolution

The final day of DERBI Foundation’s Acceleration Program focused on building long-term scale engines - partnerships, investor readiness, and leadership evolution.

We began with “Channel & Partnerships: Designing a Partner Engine That Scales,” led by Venkat Shyam. Founders explored how structured channel #strategies, aligned incentives, and ecosystem #collaborations can unlock non-linear growth beyond direct sales.

In the #Fundraising Deep Dive: #Investor-Grade Company — From Pitch to Process & Metrics That Raise Money, Ravindra Krishnappa emphasized building companies that are investment-ready by design. The session broke down traction KPIs, investors' trust, #governance discipline, narrative clarity, and process maturity.

The program concluded with “Org & Leadership for Scaling: Founder-to-CEO Transition” led by Sathyanarayana B V, followed by final reflections and key takeaways. The conversation centered on building leadership depth, creating accountable org structures, and evolving from operator to strategic decision-maker. Sathyanarayana B V also spoke about #HR Management Grid, Leadership styles, how each one of them affects and has an impact in different workplaces, and how leaders are born or lost under different #leadership style

Scaling a startup ultimately requires more than #strategy - it demands founder transformation.

We thank all our expert #mentors and participating #founders for making this acceleration journey deeply insightful and impact-driven. At DERBI Foundation, our commitment remains clear: enabling startups with the right #ecosystem, right #frameworks, and right #mentorship to scale sustainably.

Up to 15% of food produced in India perishes due to lack of refrigeration. Medicines and vaccines also depend on consistent cooling from storage to delivery. Yet refrigeration remains unaffordable to many farmers and traders due to high upfront costs. Reefer trucks running on fossil fuels add to the ecological cost of this operation as well. Currently, there exists a gap of 3.2+ million metric tonne in India’s cold-chain capacity. 

Tan90 Thermal, one of the winners of Social Alpha’s Techtonic: Innovations in Clean Energy (Edition 3), has developed a low-cost, proprietary Phase Change Material-based portable cold storage solution, offered as cooling-as-a-service, to make farm-to-fork transportation more efficient and less carbon-intensive. 
Tan90 Thermal is an example of how hands-on mentorship, product development assistance, and catalytic funding can reimagine innovation in energy access and efficiency, especially in critical sectors like food and pharma.
